messages:
mike: Heads-up — ACME reported p99 latency jump to ~18s for embeddings and some 504s. They say it started ~09:12 UTC after a config push. Stack traces show requests queued at ingress. Repro steps from customer attached.

jess: thanks. thread to triage. Mike, do we have tenant id and request ids?

mike: tenant=acme-corp, example req id=rx-8f3e. Customer repro: curl to /v1/embeddings with 1k texts in batch, 60 concurrent clients, timeout 30s. They see steady p50 but p99 spikes. Logs:
```
ingress: admit_queue_wait_ms=12345 worker_pool=fast-gpu-2 pending=512
worker: busy=true inflight=256 max_concurrency=256
```

ana: oncall alert fired at 09:15 for admissions_p99 > 10s. Looking at dashboards — worker saturation on shard 7, autoscaler didn't add nodes because pod CPU < threshold (busy waiting on io). Looks like KV cache pressure causing slower tokens per sec.

sre-bot: Incident created: I-20230425-012. Pager duty set.

jess: can we repro internally with a smaller batch size? also what's our admission controller config for tenant priority? last change was two weeks ago.

ana: reproduction run started: script that simulates 60 clients, each sending 256-token calls. Early result: pending queue grows after ~90s, admission_throttle engages then backpressure cascades.

support-ops: customer confirms they hit a background migration that started at 09:10 — heavy KV writes to metadata store from pipeline. Likely correlation.

mike: root cause hypothesis: background migration consumed worker cycles + metadata lock contention -> worker throughput drops -> requests pile up at ingress -> admission control thresholds not tuned for this workload -> high p99 and 504s.

jess: mitigation plan (short-term):
- throttle tenant acme-corp to 20 concurrent
- bump burst capacity for hosted pool for 30min
- enable fallback model variant (smaller model) for ACME
- restart affected worker pool to clear KV locks

ana: CLI commands:
```
redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant acme-corp --concurrency 20 --duration 30m
kubectl rollout restart deploy/worker-pool-shard-7
redwoodctl capacity adjust --pool hosted-fast --burst +2
```

mike: done throttle + restart. Monitoring: pending dropped from 512 -> 40, p99 down to ~1.2s. Customer notified.

support-ops: customer accepted temporary throttle, will rerun migration after window. Repro notes saved.

jess: follow-ups (postmortem actions):
- tighten admission controller rules to consider worker throughput instead of CPU only
- add a lock-monitor to metadata store to detect heavy migration ops
- add tenant-safe-mode flag to automatically apply model fallback on high p99
- run chaos test simulating metadata migration

ana: assigning tasks: @mike will own admission controller tuning, @jess postmortem writeup, @ana add autoscaler metric (tokens/sec) and lock detector.

mike: quick note — need an A/B on admission thresholds; I'll propose default: throttle when pending > 200 OR inflight/max_concurrency > 0.9.

sre-bot: Next steps checklist updated: https://ourwiki/ops/incidents/I-20230425-012

jess: closing thread once postmortem posted.
